LHX.sentence: L3Harris barely moved today, and the real question hanging over it is whether its unusually thin profit margins recover to match the bigger defense contractors — if they do, the stock's big slide becomes a bargain rather than a warning.

ASML.sentence: ASML is up nicely, and while the stock looks expensive on paper, that's a bit of an illusion — for the only company on earth that makes these chipmaking machines, the price is actually pretty normal.

LIN.sentence: Linde is having a quiet, flat week — industrial gas demand just steadily hums along under long-term contracts, which is the whole point of owning it.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is calm, with its Azure cloud business still growing fast on the back of AI demand, and a fresh earnings update coming any day now.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher had a good week as biotech funding thaws, which usually means more lab orders down the road — though the stock has already run up sharply in the past month in anticipation.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge is steady, and the main attraction here is its hefty dividend, which is near the high end of what it's paid over the past five years — a nice reward for owning this pipeline toll-collector.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow bounced again and has been leading its peers lately, as big companies and government agencies keep signing up for its workflow-automation and AI assistant tools.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore slipped a little with mining prices, but its big dividend and the steady profits from its commodity-trading arm help cushion the ups and downs of the mining side.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta is flat, and the important thing is that the actual price it charges per ton of crushed stone is still rising nicely — the headline drop in average price is just a mix quirk, not real weakness.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA is quiet, trading near the top of its year's range, helped along by a strong Mexican peso that boosts the value of this Latin American Coke bottler for US investors.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras is flat, and while its enormous dividend is comfortably covered by cheap-to-pump oil, its unusually low earnings-based price is a hint these profits may be near the top of the cycle.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk slipped a little, and notably the whole company is valued at less than it would cost to replace its fleet of ships — a sign the market is pricing in gloom about global trade.

MA.sentence: Mastercard ticked up and, unusually, is slightly cheaper than its twin Visa right now, even as people keep tapping their cards more than ever.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical-robot maker dipped today but has strongly outpaced other medical-device companies over the past month, as hospitals keep doing more operations with its da Vinci machines — and every procedure means more supplies sold.
